cases.title: Permission bundles hide whole groups, their counts and tabs; prices masked without financial access
cases.pre:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.
2. Be able to sign in as several roles, each missing exactly one view bundle in turn: no 'Work Orders: View'; no 'Part Sales: View'; no 'Customers: View'; no 'Catalog & Inventory: View'; no 'Vendor & Order Management: View'. Also a role without 'See Financial Data', and a TimeClock-only user.
3. Records exist across all eight entity types matching one term, including priced records (a part with purchase/sell price, a part sale, a work order total, a PO total and a vendor-invoice total).
cases.steps:
1. Sign in as the role missing 'Work Orders: View', search the term, and confirm no Work Orders group, count or scope tab appears.
2. Repeat for each bundle in turn: missing 'Part Sales: View' hides Part Sales; missing 'Customers: View' hides Customers AND Assets; missing 'Catalog & Inventory: View' hides Parts; missing 'Vendor & Order Management: View' hides Vendors, Purchase Orders AND Vendor Invoices.
3. Each time, confirm the hidden group leaks neither its rows nor its count, and no scope tab appears for it.
4. Sign in without 'See Financial Data', search, and confirm every price field is masked (part purchase/sell price, part-sale total, work-order total, PO total, vendor-invoice total).
5. Sign in as a TimeClock-only user, search anything, and confirm no results appear that the user is not permitted to see.
cases.exp:
1. Permission filtering follows the eight-entity bundle mapping: Work Orders → Work Orders: View; Part Sales → Part Sales: View; Customers and Assets → Customers: View; Parts → Catalog & Inventory: View; Vendors, Purchase Orders and Vendor Invoices → Vendor & Order Management: View. (A contact match rides its parent company's Customers/Vendor permission.)

2. A hidden entity group leaks neither its rows nor its count, and no scope tab appears for it.

3. Without 'See Financial Data', every price field is masked in results (part purchase/sell price, part-sale total, work-order total, PO total, vendor-invoice total).

4. A TimeClock-only user sees no results they are not permitted to see.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 9 (role-based access), read on 16 September 2026.

Note: earlier this case described a 'nine-entity' mapping including Contacts. Spec v1.3 (2026-09-01) makes it eight entities with no Contacts group; a contact match rides its parent company's permission. This case follows the current spec.

Last checked against build v26.36.7-29ca209 on 9/17/2026.

cases.title: A prefix name match ranks above a whole-word match, which ranks above a fuzzy match
cases.pre:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.
2. Seed three records of the SAME entity type that all match one query in different ways: (a) one whose primary name STARTS with the query (prefix match); (b) one where the query appears as a whole word somewhere other than the start of the name (whole-word match); (c) one that only matches through a typo (fuzzy match).
3. None of the three is an exact identifier match, so match quality alone decides the order.
cases.steps:
1. In the search box, type the shared query.
2. Read the order of the three rows within the group.
cases.exp:
The record whose name STARTS with the query ranks highest, the whole-word match ranks next, and the typo-only (fuzzy) match ranks lowest.

This reflects match quality: a prefix name match is strongest, a whole-word match is weaker, and a fuzzy match is weakest. If an exact identifier match were present it would pin above all of them.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 6.1 (match-quality component: prefix name match stronger than whole-word match, stronger than fuzzy match), read on 17 September 2026.

Note: this is the core 'best result on top' ordering and the most sensitive ranking behaviour.

cases.title: A very short query does not produce noisy fuzzy matches
cases.pre:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.

cases.steps:
1. In the search box, type a 2 to 3 letter query that is one letter off the short name; read the results.
2. Clear the input, type the longer query that is the same single edit off the longer name; read the results.
cases.exp:
The 2 to 3 letter query does NOT surface the loose typo match: short queries need a closer match to count, so noisy 2 to 3 letter fuzzy matches are avoided.

The longer query (4 or more letters) with the same single edit DOES return its fuzzy match.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 7 (edit-distance thresholds: a closer match is required for queries shorter than 4 characters than for longer ones, to avoid noisy short matches), read on 17 September 2026.
